function: above_phy (p. 1, p. 6): inverse soft-Q learning only decides IRS-user association; UAV trajectory, SIC order and power use SCA/Dinkelbach, and RIS phases are closed-form (p. 4).
notes: Reason above_phy. p. 1: "an inverse soft-Q learning-based algorithm to optimize multi-IRS multi-user association. Then, SCA and Dinkelbach-based algorithm are leveraged to optimize UAV trajectory followed by the optimization of SIC decoding order scheduling and power allocation". p. 6: the agent's action A[t] is only the binary association alpha and its state is the UAV position ("define action A[t] ... to represent binary variable alpha chosen by the agent"). The RIS phase shifts follow a closed-form optimal strategy (p. 4, eq. (10), Theorem 1), so no learned component sets the RIS phases, the power, or any beam of the aerial link, and the learning acts on user association, which the instructions list above the physical layer. Not no_learning: learning is a core part of the proposed AISLE method, not a motivation or a baseline. For the reviewer to confirm: the association also fixes how the rows of each IRS are split among its users (p. 3, J_{s,i}[t] = J_b divided by the number of users served), which could be read as allocating reflecting resources of an aerial link; I kept user association because the paper names and formulates it so (title, p. 6 Section III.A). The PDF is arXiv:2312.04786v1 and matches the DOI (same title and authors in the DOI metadata).
